title: Cost-aware phase splitter for prefill/decode with kernel hinting and fairness weights
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a cost-aware phase splitting scheduler for the prefill/decode pipeline that dynamically chooses split points and scheduling weights based on kernel-selection hints and attention-cost estimators. Goal: reduce median and tail latency for latency-sensitive requests while preserving throughput and fairness across tenants and priority tiers. The scheduler should surface clear metrics for trade-offs and enable safe rollout with canaries and automatic fallbacks to current arbiter if regressions are detected.
background: Current prefill/decode schedulers use largely static phase splits or heuristics tied to token counts. As we expand support for heterogeneous kernels (FP16/INT8/4-bit kernels) and attention optimizations (sparse attention, grouped KV caching), static policies lead to either wasted GPU cycles or increased latency tails. We need a scheduler that is kernel-aware and admits explicit fairness controls so production workloads (low-latency routes) don't starve batch/throughput-heavy routes and vice versa.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New scheduler deployed behind feature flag. 2) Benchmark: <=5% throughput regression on mixed workload compared to baseline, and median latency improvement >=10% for latency routes in test harness. 3) Fairness metric (Jain's index on token-allocated GPU time across routes) no worse than baseline threshold. 4) Rollout playbook + automatic rollback on >10% customer-facing error increase. 5) End-to-end telemetry (per-phase latency, kernel choice distribution, attention-cost estimates) wired into Console.
decision_log:
- Chosen design: hybrid split where prefill can be partially executed across optimized kernels; decode phases can be hedged across fast-quant kernels for tail reduction.
- Rejected pure latency-only preemption because it caused >15% throughput loss in batch scenarios.
- Fairness: implement proportional weighted tokens rather than strict quota to avoid starvation for large background jobs.
- Kernel hints: runtime will publish per-request kernel preference + attention-cost estimate; scheduler uses these as soft inputs, with fallback routing when incompatible.
implementation_plan:
1) Add lightweight attention-cost estimator to runtime prefill stage that outputs scalar cost and kernel affinity tags.
2) Extend scheduling API: support 'phase-split-suggestion' field and weighted fairness buckets.
3) Implement PhaseSplitter component which decides dynamic split points for prefill vs decode based on cost, latency SLO, and current queue.
4) Integrate kernel capability map (node->supported kernels) and add hedged decode code path to attempt fast kernel then fall back.
5) Add metrics (per-request: chosen split, kernel_used, attention_cost_est, phase latencies).
6) End-to-end tests + synthetic benchmark harness.
7) Feature flag rollout + canary on small customer cohort.
8) Post-rollout monitoring and gradual ramp to 100%.
implementation_notes:
- Keep estimator lightweight: single-pass linear cost model derived from sequence length, attention type, and KV cache hit rate.
- Kernel affinity tags are optional; scheduler must handle missing tags conservatively.
- To avoid noisy oscillation, apply exponential moving average on recent latencies before adjusting fairness weights.
- Use existing routing/fallback mechanisms; do not change request API surface.
- Storage of per-request telemetry must be sampled to control cost (1% by default for production).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for PhaseSplitter decision logic with synthetic cost inputs.
- Integration tests in local multi-GPU cluster: mixed workload of latency routes (short prompts), throughput routes (long generation), and background embeddings.
- Performance benchmark: run Production-like trace against baseline scheduler and compare throughput, median/tail latency, and GPU utilization.
- Chaos tests: simulate node kernel capability loss and ensure fallback paths maintain correctness and bounded latency increase.
- AB experiment: 10% of traffic vs baseline for 48 hours with monitoring checks enabled.
rollout_plan:
- Step 0: Merge behind feature flag; internal dogfood on infra cluster.
- Step 1: Canary at 1% traffic for low-risk routes (non-critical tenants) for 24h. Manual review of Console metrics.
- Step 2: Canary to 10% including some enterprise tenants with contractual SLAs; enable automatic rollback predicates.
- Step 3: Ramp to 50% with continuous monitoring for regression signals (errors, latencies, throughput).
- Step 4: Ramp to 100% if green.
- Post-rollout: 7-day monitoring window and retro meeting to capture lessons and adjust fairness defaults.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Kernel mismatch leading to increased latency when hedged path fails -> Mitigation: conservative hedging with quick fallback and circuit-breakers.
- Risk: Overcomplicating scheduler increases CPU overhead -> Mitigation: keep decision path O(1) per request and limit calls to estimator with sampling.
- Risk: Fairness weights oscillate and cause instability -> Mitigation: EMA smoothing and minimum hold time before weight changes.
- Risk: Telemetry cost increase -> Mitigation: sample telemetry at 1% and allow configurable sampling rate per cluster.
